thread:
sre-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: Inference p99 latency spike detected on /v1/stream (streaming-tail). p99 ~ 3.4s, SLO 1.5s. Triggered 1799876520. Auto-run playbook 'inference-db-deps'.

oncall-bot: Oncall: @irene — you have been paged for this incident. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/inference-db-deps

irene: I'm on it. pulling p95/p99 traces now. anyone seen a deploy in the last 30m?

alex: no deploys from product, I checked deploy-bot. last deploy to inference runtime was ~40m ago, stable.

maia: streaming metrics: error rate low, but tail latency spikes coincide with increased auth latency to auth-store (token service). p95 auth = 80ms -> 1.1s, p99 = 2.6s in the last 12m.

irene: copying logs. suspect control-plane feature flag fetch blocking in-request. Logs show synchronous FF eval for many requests: 
```
2026-03-15T19:02:13Z INFO request id=xyz feature_flag_evaluate start
2026-03-15T19:02:13Z WARN auth-store: token_fetch duration=1124ms path=/v1/token
2026-03-15T19:02:13Z INFO request id=xyz model inference start
```

alex: confirming DB slow queries too — token table read spikes and connection queue length high on auth-store db host auth-db-03.

maia: cc @devex — this looks like an auth-store read storm + rate-limiter fallback causing streaming stalls. The runtime does a sync call to control-plane to validate flags and token metadata for streaming sessions.

devex: ok. can we short-circuit FF eval? We have a config `INFER_SKIP_FF_SYNC=true` known in staging.

irene: oncall decision needed. Options: 1) enable local cache + skip sync FF eval (fast fallback) 2) increase auth-store DB pool for short window 3) rolling restart of auth-store replicas 4) route streaming to a cheaper model variant that avoids heavy per-request checks.

alex: quick mitigation I'd do: enable cached FF + increase short-term DB connections and add a temporary rate-limit on incoming streaming sessions from non-critical tenants.

maia: current impact: approx 18% of streaming requests have >2s tail, customer-facing errors minimal (no 5xx surge) but UX stalls. p95 now 650ms, p99 3.4s. We need to get p99 under 1.5s.

irene: executing mitigation steps now. Step 1: flip `INFER_SKIP_FF_SYNC=true` via remote-config canary to 10% then 50% then 100%. Step 2: bump auth-store connection pool from 120 -> 200 via k8s patch. Step 3: apply per-tenant burst limit for streaming in edge proxy to reduce load.

irene: applying canary for INFER_SKIP_FF_SYNC to 10% now (cmd):
```
kubectl -n controlplane set env deployment/controlplane-config CANARY_INFER_SKIP_FF_SYNC=true --record
```
maia: observed immediate improvement for the canary cohort — their p99 drops to ~480ms.

alex: patching auth-db pool:
```
kubectl -n auth rollout restart deploy/auth-store
# updated configmap pool.size=200
```

oncall-bot: Status update expected every 10m. Next check at 1799877130.

(deploy-bot): Notifying on-call: rollback not needed. No new inference runtime images in window.

maia: after pool bump and canary at 100% (10m), cluster-level p99 is down to 1.2s. p95 stable ~450ms. Streaming stalls rate reduced by ~75%.

irene: good. now we should add a short-lived fallback in the runtime to use cached tokens for 30s TTL to avoid token fetchs per chunk. I'll open a small patch and hotfix.

alex: quick SQL we saw: 
```
SELECT token, tenant_id FROM tokens WHERE tenant_id = $1 LIMIT 1; -- avg 1.1s during spike
```
Consider adding in-memory LRU on auth client.

devex: note for private/private deployments: if control-plane is slow, runtime config has 'ff_local_cache.enabled' that we can nudge. We'll add to runbook.

irene: customer impact assessment: no 5xx spike, but interactive sessions experienced stalls ~2-8s; likely degraded UX for customers using streaming chats. No confirmed data leakage. Impact window: 18:02-18:22 UTC. Estimated affected traffic ~12% of streaming sessions.

maia: post-mitigation tasks: - revert the temporary connection pool increase after 2 hours - add fallback token cache in runtime - add a circuit-breaker around FF sync calls - add alert for auth-store connection queue length and FF eval latency

alex: I'll follow up with infra to schedule a controlled scaling of auth-db replicas and investigate slow queries. Ticket: INF-4392.

irene: handing over to SRE lead for blameless postmortem and follow-ups. Handoff summary: mitigation completed, p99 back under SLO, temporary config changes applied (INFER_SKIP_FF_SYNC=true, auth-pool bump), customer impact noted.

maia: :thumbsup: Good job. I'll draft the incident timeline and include graphs.

irene: onboarding next oncall @alex for the remainder of the night. leaving notes in the incident doc.

oncall-bot: Handoff complete. New oncall: @alex. Reminder: run postmortem checklist and link to INF-4392.

alex: taking it. will monitor for 1h then escalate if any regressions.

(devex): small follow-up: add a runtime flag to make FF evaluation async (non-blocking) for streaming requests. I'll track with DEVEX-210.

maia: timeline note: first alert 1799876520, mitigations began 1799876560, p99 under SLO at 1799876740, full rollback of canary to stable config at 1799876800, incident declared resolved at 1799876815.

irene: resolved for now. please add any additional notes or customer pings below. :white_check_mark:
